To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
activation of mu-opiod receptors enhances electrical (and glutamate-mediated) synaptic transmission at mixed synapse on the Mauthnuer cell.

mu-opioid agonists enhance long-term electrical transmission at mixed chemical-electrical synapses on the fish Mauthner cells via a dopamine D1/2 receptor-mediated activation of postsynaptic protein kinase A.
mu-opioid receptor activation enhances electrical and glutamatic transmission at mixed synpases on the goldfish mauthner cell, but not inhibitory transmission, via the indirect action of dopamine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the modulation of electrical transmission in the brain and its possible role in the regulation of neuronal networks.
the role of gap junctional communication in the modulation of neuronal networks and the mechanisms by which it is regulated by neuromodulatory systems.
the functional significance of the opioid system on electrical synapses, and the possible involvement of dopamine in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
opioids can potentiate electrical synapses, and this is a novel finding that is relevant for the study of the opioid system and gap junctions in general.
opioid receptors are able to modulate electrical transmission at mixed electrical-chemical synapses on the fish Mauthner cell, but not at chemical or electrical synapses on the same neurons.
opioid receptors modulate electrical transmission at mixed contacts, but not at purely electrical synapses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
opioid receptors can modulate the efficacy of electrical synapses in the vertebrate brain.
opioid receptors can modulate the strength of electrical synapses in the brain.
opioid receptors are able to modulate electrical synapses in a manner similar to that of their chemical counterparts.
The main takeaway from our work is that

opioid receptors are not only involved in the control of chemical transmission but they can also affect the activity of electrical synapses, thus providing an additional level of control of neuronal network activity.
opioid receptors can regulate the strength of electrical transmission, which may be of importance in the modulation of neuronal activity in the brain.

electrical synapses are not just simple, passive conduits of electrical current, but are also capable of being modulated, and that this modulation can be used to fine-tune the overall output of neurons.
